title: request-vignette-catalog-and-priority-lens-2026-03-05
content:
Customer feedback synthesis + request vignette catalog (working draft)
Owner: Aisha Patel (CS)
Collaborators: Evan, Riley, Marta
Status: draft — notes for product/eng sync 2026-03-08

Purpose
- Rapidly surface paired customer vignettes and actionable request fragments so eng/product can evaluate small, medium, and large interventions.
- Emphasize high-frequency friction that has measurable downstream cost/latency or creates support overhead.
- Capture low-effort quick wins to unblock churn risk while larger design work is scoped.

Sources & method
- 60 support threads (Jan–Feb 2026) flagged as "inference failure" or "unexpected output" in Zendesk; sampled 3x by account tier.
- 12 post-call notes from CS+Solutions pre-sales and onboarding (Feb 2026).
- Instrumented telemetry: top-20 routes by error-rate and 95th latency from Console (Jan–Feb 2026).
- NPS follow-ups (20 respondents) and two customer interviews (fintech + enterprise SaaS).
- Heuristic mapping: map each customer quote to: symptom, immediate cost (ops/latency), root cause hypothesis, candidate fix.

Executive summary (tl;dr)
- Three clusters drive majority of actionable asks: 1) routing/fallback unpredictability, 2) cost/throughput surprises at scale, 3) tool-calling/structured output brittleness.
- There are 4 low-effort patches we can ship in a sprint to reduce support load ~15–25% for flagged accounts.
- Two mid-effort platform features (fallthrough policy editor + billing-transparent route preview) appear repeatedly in enterprise asks and should be scoped for Q2.

Vignette catalog (compact)
1) Theme: unpredictable model fallback behavior
- Customer vignette: "We had a weekend incident where requests spiked and our app started returning a cheaper quantized variant — responses lost entities and users complained. We couldn't pin rollback without digging into routing logs." — Enterprise security imagery client
- Frequency: 14 unique accounts in sample (mostly dedicated & private deployments).
- Immediate cost: escalations, downgraded quality, ~3 hours of SE time per incident on average.
- Root cause hypothesis: routing policy opaque to users; logs not surfaced at app/request level; automatic fallback triggers ambiguous.
- Candidate fixes:
  * Low-effort: add per-request /response header indicating model_variant + fallback_reason (lightweight, 1-week).
  * Mid-effort: per-account routing preview UI + canary simulation (2–3 sprints).
  * Trade-offs: header increases surface area for leaking model internals; must pair with privacy guidance.
- Suggested owner: product-hosted-api + eng-serving-runtime
- Effort estimate: low -> header (low), UI preview (medium)

2) Theme: token-cost surprises for batched streaming endpoints
- Customer vignette: "We batch user messages for throughput but token counting is off when prefixes are cached. Our billing shot up by 40% month over month." — AI-native startup
- Frequency: observed in 9 high-batch-volume accounts; telemetry confirms mismatch between inferred token cost and billed tokens in 12% of requests for these accounts.
- Immediate cost: billing disputes, quota overruns, temporary throttles.
- Root cause hypothesis: mismatch between client-side batch sizing heuristics and server-side prefix/KV cache reuse assumptions.
- Candidate fixes:
  * Low-effort: publish a short FAQ + corrected token-estimation snippet for common SDKs (2–3 days).
  * Mid-effort: telemetry flag + automated alert when expected token delta > 15% vs. bill estimate for a route (1 sprint).
  * Long-term: expose per-batch token preview API for customers to estimate cost pre-run (quarterly roadmap).
- Suggested owner: developer-experience + optimize
- Effort estimate: low -> FAQ (low), alerting (medium), preview API (high)

3) Theme: tool-calling and structured output fragility
- Customer vignette: "Our tool caller sometimes drops fields when the model returns slightly rephrased JSON. It breaks downstream ingestion and retry logic." — Mid-market conversational agent
- Frequency: 7 accounts reported repeated regressions after model upgrades.
- Immediate cost: failed downstream jobs, increased latency from retries, 0.5–1% conversion loss per affected route.
- Root cause hypothesis: brittle parser heuristics and lack of a proxied schema enforcement layer.
- Candidate fixes:
  * Low-effort: add a tolerant JSON normalization layer and explicit schema validation in Console routing rules (1 sprint).
  * Mid-effort: propose a lightweight tool-schema registry with versioned contracts (2–3 sprints).
- Suggested owner: console-and-rollouts + product-hosted-api
- Effort estimate: low->medium

4) Theme: ephemeral authentication expiration causing session failures
- Customer vignette: "We see a spike in 401s when customers move across regions or when private deployment tokens rotate — our retry logic is brittle." — Regulated enterprise
- Frequency: 11 accounts, concentrated in private deployments & cross-region traffic.
- Immediate cost: failed requests, manual token refreshes, support tickets.
- Root cause hypothesis: client SDKs do not surface token renewal hooks; private deployments may have misaligned token TTLs.
- Candidate fixes:
  * Low-effort: SDKs: expose token-refresh callback and example patterns in onboarding (1 week).
  * Mid-effort: Console: token-ttl diagnostics per-deployment + alerting when >10% of requests see 401s (2 sprints).
- Suggested owner: developer-experience + private-deployments
- Effort estimate: low->medium

5) Theme: observability gaps on per-route costs and error traces
- Customer vignette: "We spend hours aggregating logs to decide whether to switch models for a route. The console shows totals but not route-level panes by error type." — Platform team at a scale-up
- Frequency: telemetry indicates 20+ routes across 6 customers with repeated confusion.
- Immediate cost: decision latency for rollouts, higher SRE load.
- Root cause hypothesis: Console aggregates by model but not by route+error-typed slices; tracing hooks exist but are not pre-built as views.
- Candidate fixes:
  * Low-effort: add two pre-baked Console dashboards: per-route cost delta and per-route error taxonomy (2 weeks).
  * Mid-effort: tracing integration templates for common frameworks + one-click trace capture when a route crosses an error threshold (quarter).
- Suggested owner: observability + console-and-rollouts
- Effort estimate: low->high

6) Theme: onboarding friction for deduping prompt templates
- Customer vignette: "Our team had the same prompt variant in multiple services; no good way to share canonical templates across environments. Hard to run regression tests." — SMB product team
- Frequency: pervasive in smaller customers and new accounts.
- Immediate cost: duplicated work, misaligned A/B tests, accidental regressions on rollouts.
- Root cause hypothesis: no first-class prompt-template registry in Console; exporters are ad-hoc.
- Candidate fixes:
  * Low-effort: create a prompt-template import/export CLI example + docs (1 week).
  * Mid-effort: prompt-template registry with labels and versioning + link to eval sets (2–3 sprints).
- Suggested owner: developer-experience + product-hosted-api
- Effort estimate: low->medium

Quick wins (ship within 1 sprint)
- QW1: Response headers that reveal model_variant + fallback_reason (privacy reviewed). Reduces triage time. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- QW2: Short token-estimation FAQ + SDK snippet. Owner: developer-experience.
- QW3: Add tolerant JSON normalization middleware in public SDKs. Owner: developer-experience.
- QW4: Prompt-template import/export recipes + one-page console walkthrough. Owner: developer-experience.
Estimated impact: reduce support hours for sample accounts by ~15–25% and mitigate 2 of the 3 largest escalation classes.

Open questions / unresolved trade-offs
- How do we balance exposing fallback reasons (useful for engineering) vs. exposing internal model lifecycle choices to customers? Need legal/ security sign-off.
- Prioritization tension: telemetry-driven cost alerts vs. proactive UI features (which customer buys). We should A/B a telemetry-first approach for top 10 accounts.
- For private deployments, do we require a policy that token-ttl must match control-plane expectations? That could break some on-prem setups.

Suggested immediate next steps (for product+eng sync 2026-03-08)
1) Approve QW list (ship QW1–QW4). Owners assigned above. Timeline: 1 sprint for QW1/2/3 and 1 week for QW2/4 docs.
2) Product to kick off scoping for: routing preview UI and billing-transparent route preview (2-week discovery).
3) Security to review data exposure risk for model_variant headers (target: 2026-03-12).
4) CS to prepare 3 controlled customer outreach messages (top-tier customers) to preview proposed telemetry features and collect early buy-in.

Decision log
- 2026-03-01: prioritize header + SDK FAQ as immediate mitigations (agreed in CS standup).
- 2026-03-04: Console pre-baked dashboards accepted for alpha build.

Appendix: raw exemplar quotes (redacted)
- "It felt like the model switch overnight; our emails lost the subject extraction field." — anon enterprise
- "Billing surprised us — we only learned after a huge invoice. There was no easy simulation to understand cost for our batch patterns." — anon startup
- "Tool outputs changed shape after a model upgrade and our parser failed silently for hours." — anon mid-market

Notes to self
- Align with product-hosted-api on whether header string should be machine-readable (JSON) vs. compact token.
- Add a small telemetry collection to validate token-preview heuristics before public docs.

Action items (owners + dates)
- Aisha: run 3-account pilot for model_variant header by 2026-03-12.
- Evan: draft FAQ and SDK snippets by 2026-03-09.
- Riley: spin up console dashboard mockups and attach screenshots to Confluence page FEED-4983 by 2026-03-11.
- Marta: coordinate security review and collect privacy guidance by 2026-03-12.

If you want: I can split this into two artifacts: (1) a one-page customer-facing FAQ for billing/token previews and (2) an internal engineering brief that contains a proposed header format and telemetry schema.

----
End of draft.
